purpose: Original flight and full-scale tunnel propeller efficiency readings with operating conditions and installation identity.

sources.report: NACA ACR L4L07 / WR L-177, A. W. Vogeley, December 1944
sources.location: Printed pp. 12–13 Tables I–II, Figures 4–6 and text pp. 4–6.
sources.notes: Four-blade Curtiss 714-1C2-12, 12 ft 2 in, engine:propeller reduction 2:1. The slipstream survey supplies thrust. Table I values are read from the retained original scan and include independent printed rounding. Table II adds 11 indexed-text rows that pass two coefficient checks, with operating conditions retained.

sources.aircraft: Rotol RA.10046 wooden, two-blade Spitfire IX design test article
sources.report: ARC R&M 2357 / RAE Aero. 1780, A. B. Haines and P. B. Chater, June 1946
sources.location: Table 3, printed p. 7 (PDF page 8), and sections 2–3.
sources.notes: 24-ft RAE tunnel. Test article diameter 10.75 ft and two hydulignum blades. The printed propulsive thrust and torque coefficients were read from indexed original text. 25 rows agree with the printed efficiency identity within 0.005 absolute efficiency. The tabulation uses indexed text. An ambiguous OCR row is retained in the review entry. The modeled BS.543 has four RA.10061 metal blades.

series.source_location: Table I, printed p. 12, Figure 4 climb series
series.conditions: Military power / nominal 2700 engine rpm / 165 mph IAS
series.notes: IAS applies to the published flight schedule. J and both Mach numbers retain their respective forward speed definitions. Shaft coefficients, thrust coefficients and eta are the original printed readings.

series.source_location: Table I, printed p. 12, Figure 5 climb series
series.conditions: Normal power / nominal 2550 engine rpm / 160 mph IAS
series.notes: IAS applies to the published flight schedule. J and both Mach numbers retain their respective forward speed definitions. Shaft coefficients, thrust coefficients and eta are the original printed readings.

series.source_location: Table I, printed p. 12, Figure 6 climb series
series.conditions: Normal power / nominal 2550 engine rpm / 165 mph IAS
series.notes: IAS applies to the published flight schedule. J and both Mach numbers retain their respective forward speed definitions. Shaft coefficients, thrust coefficients and eta are the original printed readings.

series.aircraft: Rotol RA.10046 wooden, two-blade Spitfire IX design test article
series.source_location: Table 3, printed p. 7 (PDF page 8), 25 arithmetic-checked rows across four tip-Mach groups
series.conditions: Fixed 22 deg at 0.7 blade radius, two blades, 10.75 ft. Tip-Mach ceiling restricted by blade flutter in this tunnel configuration.
series.notes: Keep these tunnel readings separate from the installed four-blade Spitfire IX. Propulsive thrust includes the report's spinner/drag convention. Cp = 2*pi*KQ.

series.source_location: Table II, printed p. 13, selected runs; corroborating Fig. 11 and Fig. 12 data where available
series.conditions: Four cuffed Curtiss 714-1C2-12 blades. Runs 24-1 through 24-6 are the approximately 2700-engine-RPM, Cp about 0.35 high-load branch. The separate 21-series is Cp about 0.29 and run 12-1 is the reduced-RPM comparison.
series.notes: Each retained indexed table reading passes the rounded eta = J*Ct/Cp and helical tip-Mach checks. Run 24-4 has ambiguous indexed digits and remains linked at the original page.

calibration_reviews.finding: Run 20-1 reads J 0.94, Cp 0.140, Ct 0.116 and eta 0.779. The provisional OCR values J 1.00, Cp 0.165, Ct 0.132 and eta 0.799 belong to run 20-3 in Figure 7(b). The frozen import remains the record of the earlier transcription.
The reported fields transcribe to an efficiency of about 0.570 by the coefficient identity versus the indexed 0.609. The scan text does not establish which field is misread.
